title: eval-harness: integrate per-prompt regression metrics into CI hooks
author: Priya Patel
description: Context: Our eval-harness CI currently runs end-to-end prompt-set checks but only reports aggregate pass/fail. This PR wires per-prompt metrics into the CI hook so that (1) engineers can see which prompts regressed, (2) CI gating can target high-severity prompts, and (3) results are posted as annotated checks on the PR. Motivation: reduce noisy rollbacks and make regressions actionable by surfacing per-prompt delta metrics (EM/F1/average_similarity) and baseline comparisons. Changes: added a metrics exporter (eval-harness/metrics/per_prompt_exporter.py), GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/eval-harness-ci.yml) updates to publish a per-prompt JSON artifact and an annotations payload, a gating config (eval-harness/configs/ci_gates.yaml) that supports per-prompt severity levels and threshold overrides, and small helpers for formatting (integrations/cihook/formatter.py). Checklist: - [x] Add exporter and unit tests - [x] Add CI workflow and artifact upload - [x] Add gating config + defaults - [x] Wire PR annotation + formatted summary - [x] Run integration tests against staging cluster - [x] Update docs (integrations/cihook/README.md) Design notes: - The exporter emits a flat JSON array of metrics ({"prompt_id","metric","baseline","current","delta","severity"}) so downstream consumers (CI hook, dashboards) can parse without deep nesting. - Default gating semantics: CI fails only when a prompt marked severity: critical exceeds threshold OR when overall aggregate delta crosses global threshold. This reduces false positives while ensuring high-impact prompts are protected. - Metrics computed: exact_match (EM), f1, avg_embedding_sim, and nll_delta when available. - Workflow uploads \"per-prompt-metrics.json\" as a build artifact and posts a summarized annotation (table) to the PR using the existing cihook service. Migration notes: - Existing projects can opt-in by adding an entry to eval-harness/configs/ci_gates.yaml; the default file is added to the repo with conservative thresholds. - Backcompat: if no gating config is present, CI behavior remains unchanged. Security: annotations use the existing short-lived GitHub app credentials; no new secrets introduced. Testing: unit tests added under eval-harness/tests/test_per_prompt_exporter.py and an integration matrix in .github/workflows that runs on the open-source small-model staging runner. Related: ENG-2024 (per-prompt alerting), ENG-2040 (cihook annotation improvements).
